items.title: Omio to Buy Rail Europe, Consolidating Ground Transport — Exclusive
items.summary: By absorbing Rail Europe, a 5-million-ticket rail seller with 90-plus years of operator ties, Omio is consolidating one of travel's most fragmented, hard-to-book corners — and laying groundwork for when AI agents book trips, not just suggest them.

items.title: JetBlue Ties Loyalty Points to Flight Financing
items.summary: The airline's frequent flyer program was built to reward spending. JetBlue is using it as a pipeline to finance spending — and letting customers earn points for the privilege of paying interest.

items.title: Travel + Leisure Buys Into Maui and Hilton Head in $343 Million Deal
items.summary: The timeshare secret runs best on people who already said yes. So when it gets harder to land first-time buyers, buy someone else's customers.

items.title: United Airlines Raises Outlook, Higher Fares Offset $6 Billion in Added Fuel Expense
items.summary: United is betting that it will continue to see high travel demand in the second half of 2026 as it stares down at an additional $6 billion in fuel costs.

items.title: Scandic’s Dalata Deal Template Comes for Europe’s Mid-Cap Hotels
items.summary: Trading below your own bricks is an open invitation for financial interventions. For PPHE, Whitbread, and Meliá, the question is whether they're targets after Scandic's Dalata deal.

items.title: Oman and Africa Became Minor Hotels’ Safe Havens During the Iran War
items.summary: Minor Hotels didn’t wait out the Iran war in the Gulf. It grew in Oman and Africa instead.

items.title: Leadership Intelligence: Mapping the Busiest Year of CEO Turnover in Travel
items.summary: The CCO-to-CEO pipeline is hardening into a template, boards are dressing exits as retirements, and high-growth markets are importing their turnaround CEOs. One year of moves, mapped by Skift Exec Search.

items.title: What If AI Doesn’t Fix Travel’s Labor Problem?
items.summary: Travel’s AI investment is concentrated in office work while its demographic labor crisis is concentrated on the front line; the jobs aging fastest remain stubbornly physical.
